task_name: The page's half of the channel

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each one has production lines behind it. 'Lists the live sessions': SessionsClient.list() fetches '/sessions' and validates the wire shape, and useLiveSessions turns it into a loading/loaded/unavailable state the page can render. 'Subscribes to one': watch() opens new EventSource(`/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/stream`) and delivers each frame's bytes to the listener, matching the frame session-stream-route.ts writes (`data: ${JSON.stringify({ bytes })}`). 'Sends text into it': type() posts {"text":text} as json to /sessions/:id/input, which is exactly the body SessionInputRoute accepts (TEXT_FIELD = 'text', unknown fields refused). vite.config.ts gains '/sessions' so all three reach the backend in dev. No component is promised by this task's Objective or Files, so the absence of a rendered terminal is task 7's business, not a gap here.

The TDD line asks for it('the live sessions the backend lists reach the page') where a body of {"sessions":[{"id":"a1","name":"zsh"}]} answers { kind: 'loaded' } with that row. client.test.ts has that exact name; it stubs fetch with SessionsMother.oneSession().body, which is JSON.stringify({ sessions: [{ id: 'a1', name: 'zsh' }] }), and asserts resolves.toEqual({ kind: 'loaded', sessions: [{ id: 'a1', name: 'zsh' }] }). Same input, same assertion, same expected value as the sentence the plan wrote.

Four blocks, all matched name by name. Sessions.types.ts is byte-for-byte the Contract block: LiveSession, the two-member SessionsOutcome, SessionFailure {code, detail}, SessionStreamListener with onBytes/onFailure/onUnreachable and no onRefused, SessionStreamSubscription. client.ts exports SessionsClient with list(): Promise<SessionsOutcome>, watch(id, listener): SessionStreamSubscription and type(id, text): Promise<void> -- the three names, the parameter names and order, and the return shapes as declared. useLiveSessions.ts declares LiveSessionsState with the three members in the declared order and exports useLiveSessions: () => LiveSessionsState (as `const` plus `export { }`, the same shape as the useExternalTools exemplar; the exported name and its type are what the block fixes). The Current state block for vite.config.ts line 8 is honoured: API_PATHS gains '/sessions' as one entry and the eight existing entries are untouched. The contract's omission of onRefused is the plan's own, and the diff states what the brief states; what that omission costs is answered under patrones.

Four rows bear on this diff and all four are implemented with their stated value. P-2 (a frame carries bytes and nothing else): watch() reads only `bytes` out of each data frame and no 'kind' field is declared or read anywhere. P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session): SessionsClient has list, watch and type and nothing else -- no POST /sessions, no delete, no command travelling from the browser. P-8 (Spanish product copy, English everywhere else): the diff renders nothing, and every identifier, constant and test name is English. P-9 ('session-not-live' is the backend's code): the client neither compares that code nor invents it, which is the right treatment of a code the backend owns. The rest (P-1, P-4 to P-7, D-1 to D-25) are backend or later-task rows this diff does not touch.

EXEMPLARS. plan-events/client.ts: the diff matches its idiom line for line -- PATH/BYTES_EVENT/FAILURE_EVENT constants, the carriesData type guard, the settled/settle latch that closes once, an addEventListener pair and a returned { close }. external-tools/client.ts: the list() guard is the same shape (isRecord + Array.isArray + every-element predicate, `response.ok ? await response.json() : null`, catch -> { kind: 'unavailable' }), which is what the brief asked for. useExternalTools.ts: useState + useEffect + a guard against a late resolution after unmount, exported by name. SessionsMother follows ExternalToolsMother exactly (bodyOf plus named scenarios), which is what conventions/testing.md asks of a mother: 'Its methods are named scenarios'.

STYLE.MD, THE FREE-FUNCTION RULE (the implementer's declaration 1). I rule it complies. style.md says 'every function hangs off a type', and SessionsClient and SessionsMother are exactly that: named namespaces gathering their members -- the shape conventions/architecture.md itself recognises when it says 'A class nobody instantiates is a namespace, tolerated only because conventions/style.md bans loose functions'. The antipattern is 'A function at module level. Find its type.', and here the type was found and named. The one genuinely bare module-level function is useLiveSessions, and there the plan's Contract block prescribes `export const useLiveSessions: () => LiveSessionsState` verbatim -- item 3 would have flagged any other shape -- while React fixes the call shape and the named exemplar useExternalTools.ts is identical. That is a clash between a block of the plan and a document, so I declare it here instead of reporting it, and I note that CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md say this repository keeps ct's exemption for this rule, refusing it only for the language rule. No prose in the new code: zero comments, zero docstrings. English throughout, including test names, and no product copy is added.

DEFECTS.MD, RULE BY RULE. (1) Closed vocabulary: SessionsOutcome and LiveSessionsState are discriminated unions with no boolean and no optional standing in for a member -- correct. Two blemishes, both the plan's contract rather than this diff's logic: SessionFailure.code is a loose `string` where the backend owns a closed set (SessionInputOutcome: session-not-live, body-not-a-json-object, unknown-field, malformed-text), and nothing in the diff compares it by hand, so no defect is introduced there; and the dispatch in useLiveSessions.ts line 20 is a ternary whose else branch is a catch-all over SessionsOutcome, which is the one thing I report, as a low. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: none. list() returns a union and watch() returns a subscription; SessionsMother's { status, body } is a wire payload inside test scaffolding, a serialization boundary, and it is the host mother's own shape. (3) Two fields that have to agree: none. 'unavailable' carries no empty sessions array, no sentinel stands for an absence, and the `settled` latch is not a copy of source.readyState -- the browser can close the source without us settling, which is precisely the difference plan-events reads. (4) An error named for where it happens: no error type is introduced, and 'unavailable' names what happened rather than the module it happened in.

BOUNDARIES AND THE onRefused GAP (the implementer's declaration 2). The premise is right and the conclusion is not. session-stream-route.ts answers session-not-live as a plain 400 before writeHead, so the browser fires 'error' with no data and onFailure is never reached -- but a 400 before the SSE headers leaves the EventSource permanently CLOSED, while a dead backend leaves it CONNECTING and retrying. plan-events/client.ts reads exactly that distinction (`const refused = source.readyState === EventSource.CLOSED`) and the repo already pins it with a test, 'should report a refusal, not unreachable, when the browser fails the connection for good', over FakeEventSource.refuseBeforeOpen(). So a page built on this listener cannot tell a dead session from a dead backend, and cannot tell 'stop, this session is gone' from 'wait, it will come back'. Within the contract the plan fixed, the implementer had no honest way to keep that distinction: adding onRefused contradicts the Contract block, and synthesising {code:'session-not-live'} in the client would copy a decision the backend owns (conventions/decisions.md). It declared the tension in its report, which is what conventions/simplicity.md prescribes when the burden cannot be discharged. The repair is a third member of the listener's vocabulary and it belongs to the plan. Two consequences travel with it, left out of the findings for the same reason: the `if (carriesData(event))` branch has no producer today, since the sessions stream writes only bytes frames, which reads as conventions/simplicity.md's 'An unreachable check is not a check'; and the `JSON.parse(event.data) as SessionFailure` inside it is a cast at a boundary. Both exist because the Contract declares onFailure. Also declared, not reported: SessionsMother.noSessions has no caller (the brief asked for three bodies and the Tests line asked for no empty-list case), and the two halves of this wire contract are copied without a test comparing them (conventions/decisions.md), which this task could not add without writing a file outside its **Files:**.

Does not apply: the diff has no pre-existing test to weaken. Six of the seven files are new, and the only `-` line in the whole diff is the API_PATHS declaration in vite.config.ts, replaced by the same array with '/sessions' appended -- no assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten anywhere.

The promised behaviour lives in production code. Delete client.ts and useLiveSessions.ts and every one of the seven tests dies at the import. The wire parsing (isRecord/isLiveSession/every), the EventSource subscription and the POST body are all in client.ts; the loading -> loaded/unavailable transition is in useLiveSessions.ts. The scaffolding is scaffolding and asserts nothing of its own: SessionsMother only builds wire bodies, and FakeEventSource doubles the platform's EventSource, which jsdom does not provide, not the code under test. The one assertion that names a double -- expect(posting).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/sessions/a1/input', {...}) -- is on the literal request the production code sent, which conventions/testing.md prescribes at a boundary ('the literal request sent'), not on the double's own behaviour.

The seven touched paths are the seven the **Files:** line declares, and what is written inside them serves the task. vite.config.ts changes one line, appending one entry, exactly as the Current state block says; the eight existing prefixes stay, so the `### Out of scope` sentence about the eight existing endpoints is honoured. Nothing opens or kills a session (P-3), no resize, no second frame kind, no endpoint added. No refactor of a neighbouring module, no rename, no adjacent fix. There is no plan hunk in this diff -- docs/superpowers/plans is untouched, so no amendment was made and none needed judging; docs/superpowers/metrics/issue-327.jsonl shows as modified in the tree but is not staged and is not in the package.

Seven new tests, all three properties held. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep and no network -- fetch is stubbed per test and EventSource is replaced by FakeEventSource, so the same code passes today and tomorrow. Isolated: each test stubs its own global, afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals()) undoes it in both files, FakeEventSource.install() resets its own static `opened` array, the hook tests get RTL's automatic cleanup (globals: true), and no test depends on another's state or on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what list(), watch(), type() or the hook produced -- reverting the production lines of this diff makes all seven fail at the import, so none of them could pass without the code. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md reference and found nothing there to pin beyond the three: no assertion checks for the existence of a mock, no test-only method was added to production code, the mothers mirror the real wire body the backend sends rather than a partial invention, and no mock setup outweighs its test. The names are sentences that say what is guaranteed, which is what conventions/testing.md asks for.

findings.what: The hook maps SessionsOutcome to LiveSessionsState with a ternary whose else branch is a catch-all: any member that is not 'loaded' becomes 'unavailable'. conventions/defects.md asks for an exhaustive dispatch precisely so that adding a member fails visibly, and this slice is likely to add one -- the listener vocabulary is already short a member for a session the backend refused (see the patrones walk), and the day SessionsOutcome grows a 'refused' kind this line will silently report the backend as unavailable instead of failing the type check. A switch over outcome.kind with no default, inside a small function returning LiveSessionsState, makes TypeScript catch it. Low because the union is closed at two members today by the plan's own Contract block and the exemplar useExternalTools.ts collapses it the same way, so the task is right as it stands.
findings.evidence: setState(outcome.kind === 'loaded' ? { status: 'loaded', sessions: outcome.sessions } : { status: 'unavailable' })  --  conventions/defects.md: "Dispatch over it exhaustively, with no catch-all branch, so that adding a member fails visibly"
